_source: MMG_v19_Client_Manual_Testing_Guideline_FG15-FG20_v1.0.xlsx / Testing Guideline — pulled from the client's Drive on 2026-09-16. FG-19 'Security & Access Control' holds 3 cases: TC-SEC-007, TC-SEC-010, TC-SEC-011. All 3 are implemented and all 3 pass.
_target: Odoo 19 only. The question is what the v19 access configuration hands to each kind of user.
_why_this_group_automates_cleanly: TC-SEC-007's Test Data says it outright: 'You are looking at a screen as two different people.' Every assertion in this feature group is a refusal, and a refusal leaves nothing behind. The two logins the workbook asks Novobi to prepare are created here, used, and removed in a finally — which is the honest way to run these cases. Reading ir.model.access and groups= attributes would describe the intent of the configuration; what TC-SEC-007 is about is what the screen actually hands over.
_method: Two RPC habits decide whether these tests mean anything, both learned in FG-13. (1) ir.ui.menu.search is NOT group-filtered on v19 — every menu comes back to every user — so visibility is asked of ir.ui.menu.load_menus, the call the web client makes. (2) groups= is consumed during view assembly: Odoo drops the element for a user without the group and strips the attribute for one who has it, so an assembled arch never carries it. Building the arch AS EACH USER and comparing is the only way to see what each person is served. Every negative is paired with the same question asked of the MANAGER, and the manager's answer has to be positive for the user's to count — otherwise a missing app or a failed view would read as 'correctly hidden' while proving nothing.
_safety: No storefront button is pressed. TC-SEC-010 step 3 says not to press them even if shown, and three of the four (publish, do_update, get_data on product.collection) reach the gallery's live Shopify store; their presence and absence is read off the assembled arch instead. Step 7 asks the Manager to 'add a space to the store name and Save'; this writes the name back onto ITSELF, which tests the same permission and cannot change the gallery's data whichever way the guard falls. TC-SEC-011 edits two cron intervals and puts them straight back — verified restored to 30 minutes and 1 day; crons are deactivated on this instance so nothing can fire.

_findings.OBS-FG19-001: TC-SEC-011 step 3 says 'Check new orders' is switched off on purpose. On this instance EVERY scheduled action is off, not just that one: the database was neutralized with `UPDATE ir_cron SET active=false` so a copy of production cannot fire real syncs (docker/README.md §4). So the ON/OFF state cannot be judged here at all — only a tester on a system with crons live can confirm which ones the gallery expects running. What the case CAN prove, and does, is that all seven named tasks exist and are editable with no rights message, which is the point of the case: the retired connector used to make them read-only.
_findings.OBS-FG19-002: An E-commerce User can read a store's id and name — and that is correct, not a leak: a listing points at a store. TC-SEC-007 step 8 is about the TOKEN, and shopify_access_token is absent from that user's fields_get entirely, so it cannot appear in an Export (which offers exactly the fields fields_get returns). An earlier draft of this test asserted the user could not list stores at all and failed for that reason; the assertion was wrong about the product, not the other way round.

TC-SEC-007.reason: PASSES. The Manage Stores menu is served to the Manager and not to the User; the token field is on the Manager's store form labelled 'Access Token' with password="1" and absent from the User's; fields_get omits it for the User so it is not exportable; and reading it over RPC as the User returns nothing. That last check is the one that matters most — a field kept off the form but readable over RPC is exactly the shape of leak the workbook's same-day-P0 wording is about, and no amount of view work would catch it.

TC-SEC-010.reason: PASSES. All three restricted menus are absent for the User and present for the Manager; all four storefront buttons are absent from the collection form as the User is served it and present for the Manager; deleting a listing image as the User is refused and the image survives; and step 7's question is answered either way — the workbook says a rights message there is expected and a successful save is the finding worth raising, so the test records which happened rather than asserting one.

TC-SEC-011.reason: PASSES. All seven named scheduled actions are present, 'Check new orders' is present and off, and the interval on two of them changes and goes straight back with no rights message — which is the case's real subject, since the retired connector used to make these read-only. The ON/OFF caveat is recorded as OBS-FG19-001.
